blocks.title: What is Kognai?
blocks.content: Kognai is a sovereign AI runtime that powers multiple products through a shared agent swarm. Unlike traditional AI platforms that offer a single model endpoint, Kognai orchestrates 29 specialized agents across a 9-layer architecture spanning Runtime, Configuration, Adaptation, Health, Compression, Hosting, Plumber, Ecosystem, and Financial Autonomy. The platform uses a 5-tier model router called ClawRouter that intelligently routes requests from free local models (qwen3, deepseek-r1) to cloud models (Claude Sonnet, Opus) based on task complexity and budget. Kognai currently powers five products: a TikTok Content Agent for automated short-form video creation, Achiri — a culturally adaptive AI companion for Tunisia, a Founder Intelligence Agent, a Dynamic Research Instrument, and an x402 Payment Rail for agent-to-agent micropayments. The system runs on a Mac Mini M4 vault connected via Tailscale VPN to Hetzner cloud infrastructure.

blocks.title: How does the SCS-001 content pipeline work?
blocks.content: SCS-001 (Short Content System) is Kognai's automated video creation pipeline for TikTok and YouTube Shorts. The pipeline operates in six stages: Discovery scans trending topics using archive scrapers and competitor analysis. Script Generation uses LLM-powered hook optimization with templates extracted from viral transcript analysis. Video Production combines source clips with Piper TTS voiceover, FFmpeg caption overlays, and background music from a royalty-free library. Quality Control scores each video using a multi-factor rubric including hook strength, visual quality, and caption readability. Publishing manages multi-platform delivery through Telegram-based operator workflow with batch preparation. Analytics tracks post-performance metrics to feed back into topic selection. SCS-001 supports three video templates — split-screen, reaction-style, and greenscreen — with automatic niche rotation to maintain content diversity. The pipeline runs on PM2 with configurable scheduling and produces videos using exclusively free local tools.

blocks.title: What is ClawRouter and how does model routing work?
blocks.content: ClawRouter is Kognai's intelligent model routing gateway that implements a 5-tier cost-optimization strategy. Tier 0 (Nano) uses qwen3:0.6b for simple classification tasks at zero cost. Tier 1 (Local) routes to qwen3:4b for standard generation. Tier 2 (Power) uses qwen3:14b and deepseek-r1:14b for complex reasoning, still at zero cost on the Mac Mini M4 vault. Tier 3 (Cloud) escalates to Claude Sonnet for tasks requiring superior language quality, billed per call through the x402 protocol. Tier 4 (Apex) reserves Claude Opus for emergency-only scenarios. The CEO Wallet manages USDC budgets on Base, enforcing spending limits per agent and per task. ClawRouter integrates with OpenClaw's 31-skill registry, allowing agents to invoke specialized capabilities while the router optimizes for cost. This architecture keeps daily inference costs under one dollar while maintaining output quality.

blocks.title: What is Achiri?
blocks.content: Achiri is Kognai's culturally adaptive AI companion designed specifically for Tunisia. Built on the Adaptive Companion Protocol (ACP), Achiri handles natural Derja and French code-switching — the way Tunisians actually speak. The companion prioritizes personality authenticity over feature complexity, following the principle of voice before memory: conversational character must be validated before adding memory subsystems. Achiri scored 10 out of 10 in voice personality testing. The product offers a free tier accessible to all Tunisian users, with premium features priced in Tunisian Dinar (TND) to reflect local economic realities. Cultural sensitivity filters ensure responses respect Tunisian social norms and traditions. Achiri operates as a Phase 2A deployment within Kognai's product roadmap, with safety constraints embedded in durable bootstrap files following the Summer Yu Rule to survive context compaction across sessions.

blocks.title: How does x402 agent-to-agent payment work?
blocks.content: x402 is Kognai's payment protocol enabling autonomous agent-to-agent transactions using USDC on the Base blockchain. When an agent needs to invoke a cloud model or external service, x402 handles the micropayment automatically through the CEO Wallet. The protocol supports pay-per-call billing for model API requests, skill invocations through the OpenClaw registry, and inter-agent service transactions. Budget enforcement happens at multiple levels: per-agent spending limits, per-task caps, and global daily budgets managed by the CEO Wallet. The x402 Payment Rail is Kognai's Phase 4 product, designed to become the financial autonomy layer where the agent swarm manages its own operating costs. Transaction fees from external agents using the rail create a revenue stream independent of subscriptions. The protocol uses EIP-3009 gasless meta-transactions for cost-efficient on-chain settlement.

blocks.title: What is the OpenClaw skills framework?
blocks.content: OpenClaw (v2026.3.7) is Kognai's skills framework that provides 31 reusable capabilities organized across four tiers. Tier 1 Foundation skills include core operations like prompt optimization, context compression, and lossless code editing. Tier 2 Content skills power the SCS-001 pipeline with trend analysis, clip scoring, script generation, caption optimization, scheduling, and analytics aggregation. Tier 3 Intelligence skills support the Founder Intelligence Agent with market signal processing and decision support. Tier 4 Ecosystem skills handle external integrations including Stripe payments, YouTube uploads, and Telegram bot operations. Each skill is defined as a registered capability that agents invoke through ClawRouter, enabling specialization without duplication. The Skills Registry tracks invocation counts, success rates, and cost per call. Agents can compose multiple skills within a single task, and the dual-supervisor orchestration system validates skill outputs before accepting results into the pipeline.

blocks.title: How does the Kognai agent swarm work?
blocks.content: Kognai's agent swarm consists of 29 specialized agents orchestrated by a dual-supervisor system. The swarm executes sprint-based development cycles where Harvey (CEO agent) plans work, Messi (Coder agent) writes code, and Sherlock (Supervisor agent) validates outputs. Additional named agents include Guardiola for orchestration, MacGyver for DevOps, Satoshi for financial operations, and Elon for growth initiatives. Each agent has a dedicated configuration in the kognai-agents directory with an agent.yaml defining capabilities and a prompt.md providing behavioral instructions. The orchestrator script manages agent lifecycle, task assignment, and inter-agent communication through a Supabase event bus. Safety guardrails include file size guards preventing destructive rewrites of files over 2000 lines, kill switches for account bans or low performance, and the Summer Yu Rule requiring all safety constraints to exist in bootstrap files rather than ephemeral chat context.
